approved: Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would create a new statutory officer called the Head of Environment Information Australia (HEIA) to improve the quality and accessibility of national environmental data.

This officer would work inside the climate change department, gather environmental information from many sources, maintain a public online register of important data assets, and report on the state of the environment.
The minister would have to table a response to each State of the Environment report within six months and arrange independent reviews every five years.
Creates an independent statutory position to lead environmental data and reporting.
Requires regular, independent State of the Environment reports and government responses to them.
Establishes and maintains environmental economic accounts with help from the Australian Bureau of Statistics.
Sets up a public online register of national environmental information assets.
Restricts disclosure of protected information, with civil penalties for unauthorised use or disclosure.

Federal government departments, the minister for the environment, the Australian Bureau of Statistics, data custodians, scientific bodies, academic institutions, project proponents, environmental groups, state and territory regulators, and the public.

Moved the second reading of the Environment Information Australia Bill 2025, which would establish the Head of Environment Information Australia to lead improvements in national environmental data, reporting, accessibility and accountability for environmental protection and restoration.

Moved to suspend standing and sessional orders to expedite debate and voting on seven environment bills, including limiting consideration in detail to five minutes per amendment set unless extended by a minister, and moved that the question be put.

Introduced bills establishing Environment Information Australia, a framework for cost-recovery charges under the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999, and the Environment Protection Reform Bill 2025. The package would strengthen environmental protection and restoration, streamline assessments, establish national standards and create the National Environmental Protection Agency.

Moved procedural motions to suspend standing orders and set the day's business, including immediate consideration of the Environment Protection Reform Bill and related bills, specified times for second reading and remaining stages, permitted divisions after 4.30 pm, and subsequent consideration of listed Senate business.
